hints.content:
###The strategy

The perimeter of a quadrilateral is the sum of the lengths of all the sides. 

Note that $BC=DA$, so we only need to find the lengths of $\overline{AB}$, $\overline{BC}$, and $\overline{CD}.$

We can find the length of $\overline{AB}$, $\overline{BC}$, and $\overline{CD}$ using the Pythagorean theorem (or the distance formula).

###Step 1: Finding the length $AB$



[[☃ image 1]]

$\begin{align} AB^2&= {\redE{6}^2 +\redE{7}^2 } &&\text{Pythagorean theorem} \\\\
AB&= \sqrt{\redE{6}^2 +\redE{7}^2 } &&\text{Square root both sides}\\\\
&=\sqrt{36+49} \\\\
&=\tealE{\sqrt{85}}
\end{align}$

options.alt: A coordinate plane. Quadrilateral A B C D has point A at negative five, negative two, point B at one, five, point C at five, negative two, and point D at two, negative six. Sides A D and B C are congruent. A highlighted horizontal line of six units connects from point B to a highlighted vertical line of seven units to point A.

hints.content:
###Step 2: Finding the length $BC$



[[☃ image 1]]

$\begin{align} 
BC^2&= \redE{4}^2 +\redE{7}^2  &&\text{Pythagorean theorem} \\\\
BC&= \sqrt{\redE{4}^2 +\redE{7}^2 }   &&\text{Square root both sides} \\\\
&=\sqrt{16+49} \\\\
&=\goldE{\sqrt{65}}
\end{align}$

options.alt: A coordinate plane. Quadrilateral A B C D has point A at negative five, negative two, point B at one, five, point C at five, negative two, and point D at two, negative six. Sides A D and B C are congruent. A highlighted horizontal line of four units connects from point B to a highlighted vertical line of seven units to point C.

hints.content:
###Step 3: Finding the length $CD$



[[☃ image 1]]

$\begin{align} 
CD^2&= \redE{3}^2 +\redE{4}^2  &&\text{Pythagorean theorem} \\\\
CD&= \sqrt{\redE{3}^2 +\redE{4}^2 }   &&\text{Square root both sides} \\\\
&=\sqrt{25} \\\\
&=\purpleD{5}
\end{align}$

options.alt: A coordinate plane. Quadrilateral A B C D has point A at negative five, negative two, point B at one, five, point C at five, negative two, and point D at two, negative six. Sides A D and B C are congruent. A highlighted horizontal line of three units connects from point D to a highlighted vertical line of four units to point C.

hints.content:
###Step 4: Finding the perimeter

Using the lengths of all $4$ sides, we can find the perimeter of quadrilateral $ABCD$:

$\begin{align} \text{Perimeter} &= AB+BC+CD+DA \\\\
&=\tealE{\sqrt{85}}+\goldE{\sqrt{65}}+\purpleD{5}+\goldE{\sqrt{65}} \\\\
&= 5+\sqrt{85}+2\sqrt{65}
\end{align}$

###The answer

The exact perimeter of quadrilateral $ABCD$ is $5+\sqrt{85}+2\sqrt{65}$ units (approximately $30.3$ units).
